summary: Hanford sits at the geographic heart of the San Joaquin Valley as the seat of Kings County, and its most striking number might be this: the median home value of $323,600 against a median household income of $73,544 yields a price-to-income ratio around 4.4 — remarkably accessible by California standards, where ratios of 7 or 8 are routine in coastal metros. The landscape is dead-flat agricultural plain, stretching to open-sky horizons in every direction, with the southern Sierra Nevada visible on clear days to the east. The economy orbits agriculture, food processing, healthcare (Adventist Health Hanford is a major employer), and the public sector — Kings County government offices and a nearby federal facility anchor a significant share of local jobs, meaning this is not purely a bedroom community, though some commuters do make the roughly 30-mile drive south to Lemoore Naval Air Station or north toward Visalia and Fresno. Summers are serious: average daily highs pushing well into the 90s with 9.5 hours of sunshine, so life tilts toward early mornings and late evenings. The historic downtown courthouse square gives Hanford a compact center with restaurants and small shops that many Valley towns of similar size lack, though the surrounding residential grid disperses quickly into wide-lot subdivisions. Median rent at $1,196 keeps housing costs low, but the tradeoff is geographic isolation from California's coast and major metros — Hanford is a place where affordability and small-city rhythms come packaged with a two-hour drive to the nearest beach.
